title: Superlative (the longest, the most enjoyable etc.)
subtitle: the longest / the most enjoyable
summary: Learn to form superlatives with -est and most ..., and to use the right preposition after them (in a place, of a period of time).

lesson.heading: What is a superlative?
lesson.text: A superlative says that something is the most of all. We add **-est** to short words and put **most** before longer words.

examples.text: What is **the longest** river in the world?
What was **the most enjoyable** holiday you've ever had?

lesson.heading: the + superlative
lesson.text: We normally use **the** (or my/your etc.) before a superlative.

examples.text: Yesterday was **the hottest** day of the year.
The Louvre in Paris is one of **the most famous** museums in the world.
She is really nice - one of **the nicest** people I know.
What's **the best** movie you've ever seen, and what's **the worst**?

left.label: Superlative (all the others)
examples: This hotel is **the cheapest** in town.
He's **the most patient** person I've ever met.

right.label: Comparative (two things, or ... than)
examples: It's **cheaper than** all the others in town.
He's **much more patient than** I am.

lesson.heading: oldest and eldest
lesson.text: The superlative of *old* is **oldest**. We use **eldest** only about people in a family, and *oldest* is possible there too.

examples.text: That church is **the oldest** building in the town.
Are you **the eldest** in your family?

lesson.heading: in or of after a superlative?
lesson.text: After a superlative we use **in** with places, and also with organisations and groups of people (a class, a company). For a period of time (a day, a year, your life) we use **of**.

examples.text: What's the longest river **in the world**?
We had a nice room. It was one of the best **in the hotel**.
Who is the youngest student **in the class**?
Yesterday was the hottest day **of the year**.
What was the happiest day **of your life**?

lesson.heading: Superlative + present perfect
lesson.text: We often use the present perfect (**I have done**) after a superlative, especially with **ever**.

examples.text: What's the most important decision **you've ever made**?
That was the best holiday **I've had** for a long time.

lesson.text: Places take *in* (the tallest building in the city), periods of time take *of* (the happiest day of my life).

exercises.prompt: It was an awful day. It was ___ day of my life.
exercises.explanation: bad has an irregular superlative: the worst.

exercises.prompt: A straight line is ___ distance between two points.
exercises.explanation: short is a short word, so we add -est: the shortest.

exercises.prompt: What is ___ sport in your country?
exercises.explanation: popular is a long word, so the superlative is the most popular.

exercises.prompt: I wasn't feeling well yesterday, but I feel a bit ___ today.
exercises.explanation: We compare today with yesterday, so we need the comparative better, not the best.

exercises.prompt: Which is ___ - the bus or the train?
exercises.explanation: Only two things are compared, so we use the comparative quicker.

exercises.prompt: Amy and Ben have three daughters. ___ is 14 years old.
exercises.explanation: There are three daughters, so we need a superlative: The eldest (or The oldest) - eldest is used about a family.

exercises.prompt: Brazil is a very large country. It's ___ South America.
exercises.explanation: South America is a place, so the superlative takes in.

exercises.prompt: It was a very happy day. It was ___ my life.
exercises.explanation: A period of time (my life) takes of after a superlative.

exercises.statement: Spring is a very busy time for me. It's the busiest time in the year.
exercises.explanation: It's the busiest time of the year. Periods of time take of, not in.

exercises.prompt: She's a very good student. She's one of ___ the class.
exercises.explanation: one of + superlative + plural noun, and a class takes in.

exercises.prompt: Someone has just told you a joke and you think it is very funny. Say so.
exercises.answer: That's the funniest joke I've ever heard.
exercises.explanation: We often use the present perfect with ever after a superlative.

exercises.prompt: Does each superlative need in or of?

items.text: one of the best rooms ... the hotel
one of the worst experiences ... my life
